text: One single rule matters more than any button or dialog covered anywhere else in this lesson: sharing a report also shares access to its entire underlying semantic model, whether you meant to or not.

Three link types, three genuinely different access outcomes. People in your organization works for anyone internal who has the link at all. Specific people lets you name exact individuals or guests directly. And People with existing access grants absolutely nothing new — it's purely a convenience link for someone who already has access some other way.

Every single link you create also carries two optional permissions worth understanding fully. Reshare, which is on by default, lets the recipient pass that same access along to still more people themselves. Build is the genuinely bigger grant — it lets the recipient create entirely new reports of their own, built directly on top of your underlying semantic model.

Manage permissions shows you everyone who currently holds direct access, all gathered together in one single place — grant more access, review any pending requests waiting on you, or remove someone's access entirely whenever it's no longer needed.

Hiding a table or a column in your report doesn't actually stop a determined viewer from seeing that same data through the underlying semantic model itself — only genuine row-level or object-level security actually restricts it for real. Lesson 73 packages everything covered in this lesson into something considerably bigger: a full Power BI app.
